correctness.rationale: A binary start/end-bit argument reduces all nonempty codes to one of two complementary orientations. Pair compatibility is exactly non-overlap and disjoint deletion balls. A complete, unpruned increasing-index clique enumeration checks every finite code for lengths 2..10; for n=10 it generates 142 eligible oriented vertices, six cliques of maximum size nine and no larger clique, then generates precisely twelve labeled maxima and three four-member reversal/complement orbits. All twelve are individually tested on actual deletion shadows and prefix/suffix comparisons. The shipped verifier replays VERIFY_OK; independent MILP gives optimum 9. Scope is finite, and no step extrapolates to larger n.

originality.rationale: Published full-text foundational works and relevant indexed research records cover non-overlap-only, deletion-only, or permutation-alphabet combined codes, but not the exact binary ten-bit intersection maximum, twelve complete optimizers and three symmetry orbits. These results are not logical implications of the separate maxima. Index-search absence is treated as supporting context, not proof of uniqueness; residual historical risk remains.
residual_risks: An inaccessible or unindexed earlier theorem may cover the two constraints jointly, especially under alternative names such as strong synchronization or comma-free insertion/deletion correction.
Two closely related published research-record summaries were available without their complete source files; comparisons are limited to their stated claims.
Historical priority has not received independent subject-expert verification.

value.rationale: The intersection of frame-synchronizing non-overlap and one-symbol deletion correction is a natural finite-channel code design problem, not simply an arbitrary subset. At length ten the known separate maxima are 24 and 94, whereas the exact intersection maximum is 9; six oriented complete optimizers and their symmetry classes form a genuinely complete small-block classification. The exact bound and all codebooks provide benchmarks and reproducible design choices without asserting downstream physical gains.
